items.title: 2.1.2 Notation and Value of a Function (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Pichle hisse mein hum ne function ki definition parhi. Ab sawal yeh hai ke function ko likhte kaise hain, aur kisi khaas input par us ki value kaise nikalte hain? Yahi is sabaq ka maqsad hai. Saath hi hum chaar misaalon se domain aur range nikalne ka tareeqa bhi seekhenge, jo exam ka bohat pasandeeda sawal hai.
Kitab kehti hai: agar variable \(y\), variable \(x\) par is tarah depend kare ke \(x\) ki har value se \(y\) ki bilkul ek value tay ho, to hum kehte hain "\(y\), \(x\) ka function hai".

Swiss mathematician Euler (1707-1783) ne is jumle "\(y\) is a function of \(x\)" ko chhota kar ke likhne ka symbolic tareeqa diya: \(y = f(x)\). Ise parhte hain "\(y\) is equal to \(f\) of \(x\)". Yaani har dafa poora jumla likhne ki bajaye sirf \(f(x)\) likh dete hain.

Function ko ek computing machine (hisaab karne wali machine) samjhiye jis ka naam \(f\) hai. Yeh ek input \(x\) leti hai, us par koi kaam karti hai, aur bilkul ek output \(f(x)\) deti hai. Is output \(f(x)\) ko \(x\) par \(f\) ki value, ya \(f\) ke under \(x\) ki image (aks) kehte hain. Aksar output ko ek hi harf, jaise \(y\), se likhte hain: \(y = f(x)\).

blocks.alt: A horizontal line with arrowheads passes through a box marked Function f. Left of the box: Input x; right of the box: Output f(x). Below the box: Computing Machine.

blocks.text: Is tasveer ko apne calculator se jor kar dekhiye. Calculator par \(x^{2}\) wala button ek function machine hai: aap 5 daalte hain, 25 nikalta hai. Aap jitni dafa bhi 5 daalein, hamesha 25 hi nikle ga; kabhi 25 aur kabhi 26 nahin. Function ki yahi pehchaan hai: ek input par hamesha bilkul ek, aur hamesha wahi, output. Agar koi machine ek hi input par kabhi kuch aur kabhi kuch de, to woh function nahin kehlaye gi.

Variable \(x\) ko \(f\) ka independent variable (azaad variable) aur \(y\) ko dependent variable (munhasir variable) kehte hain. Ab se hum sirf aise functions lenge jin ke variables real numbers hon, aur kahenge ke \(f\) ek real valued function of real numbers hai.
bold: real valued function of real numbers

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Sab se pehle ek ghalat fehmi door karte hain: \(f(x)\) ka matlab "\(f\) zarb \(x\)" NAHIN. Yeh ek naam hai: "jab input \(x\) ho to \(f\) ka output".
Value nikalne ka tareeqa: rule mein jahan jahan \(x\) hai, wahan diya hua input brackets ke saath rakh dein. Maslan \(f(x) = 3x + 2\) ho to
\[f(4) = 3(4) + 2 = 14\]
Yani \(f\) ke under \(4\) ki image \(14\) hai.
Input koi expression bhi ho sakta hai: \(f(a + 1) = 3(a + 1) + 2 = 3a + 5\).
Machine wali tasveer yaad rakhein: \(x\) ko hum khud chunte hain, is liye woh "independent" hai; \(y\) machine se nikalta hai aur \(x\) par depend karta hai, is liye "dependent" hai.

Ab kitab ki pehli misaal dekhte hain. Is mein koi naya concept nahin, sirf substitution ki mashq hai, lekin exam mein yahi chhote sawal aksar ghalat ho jate hain: kahin bracket chhoot jata hai, kahin minus ka sign. Is liye har step aahista aur saaf likhenge.

blocks.title: Example 1
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^{3} - 2x^{2} + 4x - 1\).
To find: \(f\) ki values \(0\), \(1\), \(-2\), \(1 + x\) aur \(\frac{1}{x}\) par.
Method: sab se pehle samajh lein ke yeh sirf substitution (rakhne) ka sawal hai. Har \(x\) ki jagah diya hua input brackets mein rakhna hai, phir simplify karna hai. Pehle teen parts mein number hain, aakhri do mein expressions; tareeqa wahi hai.

(i) \(f(0)\) nikalein
\[f(0) = 0^{3} - 2(0)^{2} + 4(0) - 1\]
\[= 0 - 0 + 0 - 1\]
\[f(0) = -1\]
Kyun: jis term mein bhi \(x\) hai woh \(0\) ban jati hai; sirf constant \(-1\) bachta hai. Is liye kisi polynomial ka \(f(0)\) hamesha us ka constant term hota hai; yeh chhota sa shortcut yaad rakhein.

(ii) \(f(1)\) nikalein
\[f(1) = (1)^{3} - 2(1)^{2} + 4(1) - 1\]
\[= 1 - 2 + 4 - 1\]
\[f(1) = 2\]
Kyun: \(1\) ki har power \(1\) hi hai, is liye har term sirf apna coefficient ban jati hai. Yani \(f(1)\) = tamam coefficients ka jama: \(1 - 2 + 4 - 1 = 2\).

(iii) \(f(-2)\) nikalein
\[f(-2) = (-2)^{3} - 2(-2)^{2} + 4(-2) - 1\]
\[= -8 - 2(4) - 8 - 1\]
\[= -8 - 8 - 8 - 1\]
\[f(-2) = -25\]
Kyun: bracket sign ko number ke saath rakhta hai. \((-2)^{3} = -8\), kyun ke odd power par minus qaim rehta hai; \((-2)^{2} = 4\), kyun ke even power par minus khatam ho jata hai.
Dhyan dein: bracket ke baghair \(-2^{2}\) likhenge to calculator bhi \(-4\) dega, jo ghalat hai.

(iv) \(1 + x\) rakhein
\[f(1 + x) = (1 + x)^{3} - 2(1 + x)^{2}\]
\[\quad + 4(1 + x) - 1\]
Kyun: poora input \(1 + x\) ek package hai jo \(x\) ki jagah aa raha hai, is liye use bracket mein band rakhna zaroori hai. Bracket hata diya to power sirf aakhri term par lagegi aur jawab bigar jayega.

(iv) Milti julti terms jama karein
\[= 1 + 3x + 3x^{2} + x^{3} - 2 - 4x\]
\[\quad - 2x^{2} + 4 + 4x - 1\]
\[f(1 + x) = x^{3} + x^{2} + 3x + 2\]
Kyun: ek ek power alag gin lein taa ke koi term na chhoote: \(x^{3}\) sirf ek; \(x^{2}\): \(3 - 2 = 1\); \(x\): \(3 - 4 + 4 = 3\); constants: \(1 - 2 + 4 - 1 = 2\).

(v) \(f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\) nikalein, \(x \ne 0\)
\[f\left(\tfrac{1}{x}\right) = \left(\tfrac{1}{x}\right)^{3} - 2\left(\tfrac{1}{x}\right)^{2}\]
\[\quad + 4\left(\tfrac{1}{x}\right) - 1\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{x^{3}} - \dfrac{2}{x^{2}} + \dfrac{4}{x} - 1\]
Kyun: \(\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)^{n} = \frac{1}{x^{n}}\), kyun ke \(1\) ki har power \(1\) hi rehti hai. Shart \(x \ne 0\) is liye lagayi ke \(\frac{1}{0}\) defined nahin.

Tasdeeq:
Ab jawab ko check karte hain. (iv) ke jawab mein \(x = 0\) rakhein: \(0 + 0 + 0 + 2 = 2\). Yeh \(f(1 + 0) = f(1) = 2\) ke barabar hona chahiye. Sahi!
(v) ke jawab mein \(x = 1\) rakhein: \(1 - 2 + 4 - 1 = 2\), jo \(f(1) = 2\) hai. Sahi!
Yeh chhota sa check exam mein bhi ek minute mein ho jata hai aur expansion ki ghalti pakar leta hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab Example 1 ke sawal mein function ke minus signs chhaapna bhool gayi hai: wahan \(x^{3}\ \ 2x^{2} + 4x\ \ 1\) chhapa hai. Kitab ka apna hal \(f(x) = x^{3} - 2x^{2} + 4x - 1\) use karta hai, aur yahi sahi function hai. Is ke ilawa kitab ke hal mein aakhri part par dobara "(iv)" likha hai; asal mein yeh part (v), yani \(f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\), hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Domain kaise nikalein? Aksar sawal mein sirf formula diya hota hai, domain nahin. Us waqt domain ka matlab hai: woh tamam real \(x\) jin par formula ka koi matlab banta ho. Tareeqa: tamam real numbers se shuru karein, phir woh \(x\) nikaal dein jin par formula toot jata hai. Do khatre ki jagahein yaad rakhein:
1. Denominator kabhi \(0\) nahin ho sakta.
2. Square root (even root) ke andar wali miqdaar \(\ge 0\) honi chahiye.
Range kaise nikalein? Khud se poochhein: "kaun se outputs \(y\) waqai aa sakte hain?". Achha tareeqa yeh hai: \(y = f(x)\) likhein, \(x\) ko \(y\) ki shakal mein hal karein, aur dekhein ke kin \(y\) ke liye yeh \(x\) real hai aur domain mein hai.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.problem: Find the domain and range of \(f(x) = x^{2}\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^{2}\).
To find: domain (jaiz inputs) aur range (jo outputs waqai aate hain).
Method: pehle dekhein ke kya koi real \(x\) nikaalna parega; phir sochein ke \(x^{2}\) kaun kaun si values le sakta hai.

Domain
Har real number ka square nikal sakta hai; formula mein na denominator hai, na root.
\[\text{Domain } f = \mathbb{R}\]
Kyun: kisi bhi real \(x\) par formula nahin toot'ta, is liye koi value nikaalni nahin parti.

Range
Har real \(x\) ke liye \(x^{2} \ge 0\).
Aur har \(y \ge 0\) tak pahuncha ja sakta hai: \(x = \sqrt{y}\) lein, to \(f(\sqrt{y}) = y\).
\[\text{Range } f = [0, \infty)\]
Kyun: square kabhi negative nahin hota (minus zarb minus bhi plus), is liye negative numbers output nahin ban sakte. Aur har non-negative number apne square root ka square hai, is liye woh sab output bante hain.

Tasdeeq:
\(f(-3) = 9 \ge 0\), \(f(0) = 0\), \(f(\sqrt{5}) = 5\). Koi real \(x\) aisa nahin jis se \(x^{2} = -1\) bane. Is liye range sirf \(0\) aur us se bare numbers hain.
blocks.answer: Domain \(f\) = tamam real numbers; Range \(f\) = tamam non-negative real numbers \(= [0, \infty)\).

blocks.title: Remember!
blocks.text: Intervals do qisam ke hote hain: open interval aur closed interval. Open interval \((a, b)\) mein kinare (endpoints) shaamil nahin hote. Closed interval \([a, b]\) mein kinare shaamil hote hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Agli misaalon mein interval notation aayegi, is liye ise abhi pakka kar lein:
\((2, 5)\) ka matlab \(2 < x < 5\) (kinare bahar); \([2, 5]\) ka matlab \(2 \le x \le 5\) (kinare andar).
\([0, \infty)\) ka matlab \(x \ge 0\). \(\infty\) koi number nahin, sirf "hamesha barhte jao" ka ishara hai; is liye us ke saath hamesha gol bracket aata hai.
\((-\infty, \infty) = \mathbb{R}\), yani tamam real numbers.
\(\cup\) (union) do intervals ko jorta hai: \((-\infty, -3] \cup [3, \infty)\) ka matlab \(x \le -3\) ya \(x \ge 3\).
\(\mathbb{R} - \{-2, 2\}\) ka matlab: tamam real numbers siwaye \(-2\) aur \(2\) ke.

Example 3 thora mushkil hai, kyun ke yahan range seedhi nazar nahin aati. Domain to aasan hai (denominator ka khayal), lekin range ke liye humein ulta chalna parega: output \(y\) se input \(x\) tak. Yeh tareeqa aage bhi bohat kaam aayega, is liye ise dhyan se samjhiye.

blocks.title: Example 3
blocks.problem: Find the domain and range of \(f(x) = \dfrac{x}{x^{2} - 4}\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \dfrac{x}{x^{2} - 4}\).
To find: domain aur range.
Method: yeh fraction hai, is liye domain ke liye woh \(x\) nikaalne hain jin par denominator zero ho. Range ke liye \(y = f(x)\) likh kar \(x\) ko hal karenge aur dekhenge ke kin \(y\) ke liye real \(x\) milta hai.

Domain: denominator kahan zero hai?
\[x^{2} - 4 = 0\]
\[x = 2 \text{ ya } x = -2\]
\(x = 2\) aur \(x = -2\) par \(f(x)\) defined nahin. Is liye
\[\text{Domain } f = \mathbb{R} - \{-2, 2\}\]
Kyun: zero se taqseem (division) ka koi matlab nahin. Baqi har real \(x\) par fraction ki ek real value banti hai.

Range: \(y = f(x)\) likh kar fraction khatam karein
\[y = \dfrac{x}{x^{2} - 4}\]
\[y(x^{2} - 4) = x\]
\[x^{2}y - 4y = x\]
\[x^{2}y - x - 4y = 0\]
Kyun: humein \(x\) ko \(y\) ki shakal mein chahiye. Cross-multiply karne se aisi equation banti hai jo \(x\) mein quadratic hai; yahan \(y\) ko sirf ek number samjhein.

\(x\) mein quadratic hal karein
Yahan \(a = y\), \(b = -1\), \(c = -4y\):
\[x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^{2} - 4ac}}{2a}\]
\[b^{2} - 4ac = (-1)^{2} - 4(y)(-4y)\]
\[= 1 + 16y^{2}\]
\[x = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 16y^{2}}}{2y},\ y \ne 0\]
Kyun: quadratic formula tab hi lagta hai jab \(a \ne 0\), yani \(y \ne 0\). \(y = 0\) wala case hum alag se dekhenge.
Dhyan dein: \(-4(y)(-4y) = +16y^{2}\); do minus mil kar plus bante hain.

Har \(y \ne 0\) par real \(x\) milta hai
Har real \(y\) ke liye \(1 + 16y^{2} > 0\), is liye square root real hai aur \(x\) har \(y \ne 0\) par defined hai.
Aur yeh \(x\) kabhi \(\pm 2\) nahin hota: agar \(x = \pm 2\) ho to equation \(y(x^{2} - 4) = x\) ban jati \(0 = \pm 2\), jo ghalat hai.
Kyun: \(16y^{2}\) kabhi negative nahin, is liye \(1 + 16y^{2}\) kam az kam \(1\) hai. Doosri baat is liye zaroori hai ke jo \(x\) mila woh domain mein hona chahiye; kitab yeh baat nahin likhti, lekin poori daleel ke liye yeh chahiye.

\(y = 0\) wala case
\[0 = \dfrac{x}{x^{2} - 4} \Rightarrow x = 0\]
\[f(0) = 0\]
Kyun: fraction tab hi zero hoti hai jab us ka numerator zero ho. Yani \(0\) bhi output hai (input \(0\) se).

Natija
Har real number \(y\) output banta hai.
\[\text{Range } f = (-\infty, \infty)\]

Tasdeeq:
\(y = \frac{1}{3}\) lein: equation \(x^{2}y - x - 4y = 0\) ko 3 se zarb dene par \(x^{2} - 3x - 4 = 0\), yani \((x - 4)(x + 1) = 0\), \(x = 4\) ya \(x = -1\).
\(f(4) = \frac{4}{16 - 4} = \frac{1}{3}\) aur \(f(-1) = \frac{-1}{1 - 4} = \frac{1}{3}\). Sahi! Dono inputs se wohi output aaya.
blocks.answer: Domain \(f = \mathbb{R} - \{-2, 2\}\) (tamam real numbers siwaye \(-2\) aur \(2\) ke); Range \(f\) = tamam real numbers \(= (-\infty, \infty)\).

blocks.text: Example 4 mein square root aa gaya hai. Yahan domain ka faisla ek inequality karti hai, aur use hal karne ka sab se aasan tareeqa critical points aur test values ka hai. Yeh tareeqa aap ne pichli classes mein shayad nahin dekha, is liye har qadam ki wajah bhi saath likhi hai.

blocks.title: Example 4
blocks.problem: Find the domain and range of \(f(x) = \sqrt{x^{2} - 9}\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \sqrt{x^{2} - 9}\).
To find: domain aur range.
Method: square root tab hi real hota hai jab us ke andar wali miqdaar \(\ge 0\) ho. Yeh inequality hum critical points aur test values se hal karenge.

Real square root ki shart
\[x^{2} - 9 \ge 0 \quad \text{...(i)}\]
Kyun: negative number ka square root real number nahin hota, aur hamara \(f\) real valued function hai. Is liye sirf woh \(x\) chalenge jin par andar wali miqdaar zero ya positive ho.

Critical points
\[x^{2} - 9 = 0\]
\[x = \pm 3\]
Yeh do points number line ko teen hisson mein baant dete hain: \(x < -3\), \(-3 < x < 3\), \(x > 3\).
Kyun: \(x^{2} - 9\) apna sign sirf wahin badal sakta hai jahan woh zero ho. Is liye har hisse ke andar sign ek jaisa rehta hai.

Har hisse mein ek value test karein
(i) mein \(x = -4\): \(16 - 9 \ge 0\) (True)
(i) mein \(x = 0\): \(0 - 9 \ge 0\) (False)
(i) mein \(x = 4\): \(16 - 9 \ge 0\) (True)
Kyun: har hisse mein sign ek jaisa hai, to ek hi test value poore hisse ka faisla kar deti hai. Is se lambi algebra bach jati hai.

Domain
Bahar wale dono hisse chalte hain, aur \(x = \pm 3\) par \(0 \ge 0\) (True), is liye yeh bhi shaamil hain.
\[\text{Domain } f = (-\infty, -3] \cup [3, \infty)\]
Kyun: \(\pm 3\) par square bracket, kyun ke yeh kinare \(\ge\) ko poora karte hain.
Dhyan dein: sirf \(x \ge 3\) likh dena aam ghalti hai; \(-4\), \(-5\) jaise numbers bhi chalte hain.

Range
Domain par \(x^{2} - 9\) ki sab se chhoti value \(0\) hai (jab \(x = \pm 3\)):
\[y = \sqrt{0} = 0\]
Jaise jaise \(|x|\), 3 se aage barhta hai, \(x^{2} - 9\) barhta barhta \(+\infty\) ki taraf jata hai, is liye \(y\) bhi \(+\infty\) tak barhta hai.
\[\text{Range } f = [0, \infty)\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{\ }\) ka nishan hamesha non-negative root deta hai, is liye \(y \ge 0\). Aur \(x^{2} - 9\) zero se upar ki har value leta hai, is liye har \(y \ge 0\) tak pahunch hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(f(5) = \sqrt{25 - 9} = 4\) aur \(f(-5) = 4\): domain ke inputs non-negative output dete hain.
\(f(0) = \sqrt{-9}\) real nahin, is liye \(0\) ka domain se bahar hona bilkul durust hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Ab ek chhoti misaal hum khud karte hain (yeh kitab ka sawal nahin): \(g(x) = \dfrac{1}{x - 1}\) ka domain aur range.
Domain: denominator \(x - 1 = 0\) jab \(x = 1\). Is liye domain \(= \mathbb{R} - \{1\}\).
Range: \(y = \frac{1}{x - 1}\) se \(x - 1 = \frac{1}{y}\), yani \(x = 1 + \frac{1}{y}\), jo har \(y \ne 0\) par real hai. Aur \(y = 0\) kabhi nahin aata, kyun ke \(1\) ko kisi cheez se taqseem kar ke zero nahin milta. Range \(= \mathbb{R} - \{0\}\).
Tasdeeq: \(y = 2\) ke liye \(x = \frac{3}{2}\), aur \(g\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{1/2} = 2\). Sahi!

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(f(x) = x^{3} - 2x^{2} + 4x - 1\) (Example 1 wala) ho to \(f(2)\) kya hoga?
Jawab: \(8 - 8 + 8 - 1 = 7\).
Aur \(h(x) = \sqrt{x - 4}\) ka domain kya hai? Jawab: \(x - 4 \ge 0\), yani \([4, \infty)\).

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Domain aur range ke sawal mein aakhri jawab hamesha set ya interval notation mein likhein, aur wajah bhi likhein ke points kyun nikale ("\(x = \pm 2\) par denominator zero", "negative number ka square root real nahin"). Kinaron ko zaroor check karein: shaamil hon to square bracket, warna gol bracket.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(y = f(x)\) parhte hain "\(y\) equals \(f\) of \(x\)" (Euler ki notation); \(f(x)\) ko \(x\) ki value ya image kehte hain.
2. \(x\) independent variable, \(y\) dependent variable.
3. \(f(a)\) nikalne ke liye har \(x\) ki jagah \((a)\) bracket ke saath rakhein.
4. Domain: woh \(x\) nikaal dein jo denominator ko zero karein ya square root ke andar negative number dein.
5. Range: \(y = f(x)\) ko \(x\) ke liye hal karein aur dekhein kin \(y\) par real \(x\) (domain mein) milta hai.
6. Open interval \((a, b)\): kinare bahar; closed \([a, b]\): kinare andar.
7. Polynomial ka \(f(0)\) us ka constant term, aur \(f(1)\) coefficients ka jama hota hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(f(x)\) ko \(f \times x\) samajhna.
2. Substitution mein bracket chhor dena: \(x^{2}\) mein \(-2\) rakhein to \((-2)^{2} = 4\), \(-2^{2} = -4\) nahin.
3. \(f(1 + x)\) mein \(-2(1 + x)^{2}\) ko \(-2 + 2x + x^{2}\) likh dena; \(-2\) har term ko zarb karta hai, is liye \(-2 - 4x - 2x^{2}\).
4. \(\sqrt{x^{2} - 9}\) ka domain sirf \(x \ge 3\) likhna; \(x \le -3\) wala hissa bhi chalta hai.
5. \(\infty\) ke saath square bracket lagana; \(\infty\) number nahin, is liye hamesha gol bracket.
6. Range nikalte waqt \(y = 0\) jaisa alag case bhool jana.
